newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bouygues shares up after analysts briefing.
newsitem.headline: Bouygues shares up after analysts briefing.

text.p: Shares in French construction company Bouygues were up sharply on Tuesday after analysts were told that Bouygues Telecoms would make a positive contribution to the group's results in the year 2001.
Bouygues shares were up 3.38 percent to 550 francs at 1130 GMT while the overall CAC-40 index was up 1.29 percent.

Analysts said they were reassured during a Monday news conference by chairman Martin Bouygues who said that Bouygues Telecoms was expected to contribute 350 million francs to the group's results in 2001.
Bouygues Telecoms was expected to make negative contributions to the group's results every year until then, the chairman said.
"It's reassuring to know that Bouygues has a clear strategy in telecommunications," one analyst said.
Analysts said they appreciated Bouygues' desire to develop its activities in the sector at an appropriate pace.
They also said they believed Bouygues shares to be undervalued, with a net asset value seen at 600 to 650 francs per share.
French brokerage Oddo said it revised upwards its profit forecast for the group to 35.1 francs per share from 20.4 francs per share previously.
